title: REPORT on public procurement
part_text: Cf. whereas recently adopted legislative instruments in the area of social policy, such as Directive (EU) 2022/2041 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on adequate minimum wages in the European Union1a and Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 to strengthen the application of the principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency and enforcement mechanisms (Pay Transparency Directive)1b, include provisions on cross-referencing public procurement legislation aiming, respectively, at strengthening the enforcement of the social clause or adding new exclusion grounds; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 1a OJ L 275, 25.10.2022, p. 33, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2041/oj. 1b OJ L 132, 17.5.2023, p. 21, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/970/oj.
